scores.evidence: a SQL Server distributed availability group, or the managed service's link feature... It keeps ID values and can run in reverse for failback
scores.rationale: Replication mechanics, drain-and-promote cutover, HL7 SIU/ADT roles, message control IDs for dedup, HIPAA citations and NIST 800-88 are all accurate, with uncertain capabilities honestly flagged as assumptions with fallbacks.

scores.evidence: Pause on saving bookings at cutover | ≤ 60 s... If any pause counts as downtime, see the revisit trigger
scores.rationale: It solves exactly the stated problem, confronts the ambiguity of 'no downtime' head-on with a named decision owner, and is clearly buildable by a realistic hospital IT team with explicit deferrals.

scores.evidence: On-prem database is the system of record until Phase 5. Then the cloud database is, with reverse replication to on-prem
scores.rationale: Write ownership, data ownership and routing are defined at every phase, the single-writer decision is honored in every section, and cross-cutting concerns are handled uniformly per phase with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: V2... Database calls per transaction × measured round-trip time as a forecast, then a 10-business-day pilot clinic
scores.rationale: Eight validation gates each have a hypothesis, method, labeled threshold, evidence artifact and a stated failure branch; the riskiest assumptions (latency, replication fidelity, cutover pause) are tested before commitment and reconciliation continues post-cutover.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION: staff will accept one slow save. Confirm with the Director of Patient Access before Phase 4
scores.rationale: Every figure is labeled REQUIREMENT, ASSUMPTION, BASELINE or UNKNOWN with a named confirmer, missing inputs are ranked by how much they would change the plan, and each decision has a revisit trigger.

scores.evidence: Appointments that are silently lost, duplicated or double-booked during coexistence or cutover... A silent data error is not caught by anything
scores.rationale: The hardest domain failures (silent appointment loss, double-booking, interface message loss/duplication, replication divergence, link and zone failure) each get concrete detection (hashes, control-ID counts, synthetic bookings) and rehearsed recovery with explicit rollback triggers.

scores.evidence: Operational complexity | Same on-call team; managed database; no new cluster to run ourselves
scores.rationale: Terraform/CI deployment with exercised rollback, domain-meaningful signals (replication delay, queue depth, synthetic booking alerts), updated on-call runbooks and a stated staffing constraint make operations sized to a realistic team.

scores.evidence: Compare run cost to budget, then commit reserved capacity
scores.rationale: Cost is gated before capacity commitment and no figures are invented, but the dominant drivers (dual-running, links, managed DB tier, engineering time) and their growth with usage are never enumerated or estimated.

scores.evidence: Phase 6: Decommission (point of no return)... Rollback: none after reverse replication stops. V7 guards this
scores.rationale: Decisions are explicitly classified R1–R3, the irreversible ones (consistency model, PHI boundary, data gravity, decommission) get the most validation and guards, exit paths exist (open-format archive, reverse replication), and reversible choices are made quickly as defaults.

scores.evidence: App servers: rehost, same build and version on cloud VMs... No upgrades combined with the move
scores.rationale: Pure rehost with no concurrent re-architecture or upgrades, an explicit deferred list with trigger conditions for each, and every component justified by the zero-downtime, PHI-safety need.

scores.evidence: Start long-lead items on day one: BAA, security risk analysis, vendor support statement, network link orders
scores.rationale: Phases are ordered by validated dependencies with concrete first steps, checkable exit criteria per phase, and explicit contingency branches (e.g. 'If V2 failed: step 5 is dropped') so a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: PHI only in services covered by the BAA, in US regions, on private endpoints. Logs that may hold PHI are classified as PHI
Sources: interface engine routes, 30+ days of database connection logs covering a month-end, firewall flow logs, SQL Agent and other scheduled jobs, DNS lookups
At least 14 days of replication covering a month-end... Hourly reconciliation (row counts per table, hash per appointment ID)
Only one writable database at any moment. No two-way, multi-writer replication. Cutover is a brief, drained save pause
At least two full rehearsals of the exact runbook on a production-sized copy, each with a full rollback
Two redundant private links (ExpressRoute or Direct Connect type), with an IPsec VPN as a third path
replay 2 × the peak-hour workload; take a zone down, fail the database over, cut one network link, restore from backup
Admin access through Entra with MFA... Break-glass access audited; check the access review after cutover
replay 2 × the peak-hour workload... then a 10-business-day pilot clinic
Put the change freeze in place... Pick the lowest-volume window from the baseline... communications plan for staff and help desk
Software vendor's written support for the target cloud and managed database... Wipe the media to NIST SP 800-88 and keep the certificates

traps.evidence: Move app servers first (users routed in waves by the hospital reverse proxy, database still on-prem), then move the database in one gated cutover
Only one writable database at any moment. No two-way, multi-writer replication
No PHI goes to tools not covered by the BAA... Test each interface in a cloud test environment with test data only
100% of inventory items pass a test signed by their owner. 0 messages lost or duplicated (counted by message control ID)
Re-architecture (breaking the app into services...) Brought forward if V4 shows one database or the app design cannot meet 2 × peak

note: An exceptionally rigorous zero-downtime migration plan — single write authority, labeled assumptions, rehearsed rollback and gated validation throughout; its only material weakness is thin cost-driver analysis.
